note: Finding: Planned.cap gives the row, loop and cubic/quartic weighted sums with summability for the chosen arrays, which carry no p or beta index, for every N and m<=N. [M]'s last claim, the same bounds at a larger width w'>w^path with A'>=A^path, is absent: Installed.uses, Scheduling.narrower and geared all move only to widths below the stage width.

structure Planned (M : Kin C O) {s : Supply.Sheet G} {ŵ : Supply.Rolls s} (Q : PostCost ŵ) : Prop where
  stage : s.profile = a.clock.stage
  lengths : ŵ.L=a.clock.factor
  links N m : m ≤ N → Attached (C.H N m) (M.path N m)
  cap N m : m ≤ N →
    let j:=a.params m
    (M.path N m).Bounds j.clip j.width j.paths (a.clock.loopCap m)
  peak N p : ∀ j, j ≤ 4 → SameJet j (fun x => mainTerm (a.params N).clip (M.path N N) (represent (x:fieldDir G (a.S.side N p) 1)))
      (fun x => Wilson.energy (represent x))
  initial N b : ( (M.path N N).loop b).coeff=0
  gap N m p : m < N → ∀ F : Forest (a.clock.op m p).ratio,
      PriceGap F (a.params (m+1)).clip (M.path N (m+1)) (Q.η (a.clock.J (m+1)))
  critical N m p : m < N → ∀ F : Forest (a.clock.op m p).ratio,
      Critical F (a.params (m+1)).clip (M.path N (m+1)) (M.stationary N m p F) ∧
        Guessed F (installed (a.clock.op m p).ratio (C.towers N m).A0) (M.stationary N m p F)
  classicalPart N m p : m < N → ∀ F : Forest (a.clock.op m p).ratio,
    ClassicalMatch F (a.params (m+1)).clip (a.params m).clip (M.path N (m+1)) (M.path N m) (M.stationary N m p F)
  kinetic N m : m < N → |M.alpha N m + G.slopeConstant*Real.log (a.S.block m).val| + 1 ≤ (a.params (m+1)).drift
  retains N m p : m < N →
    let j:= a.clock.J (m+1)
    ∀ F : Forest (a.clock.op m p).ratio,
      FiniteBound F (M.path N (m+1)) (M.path N m) (a.params (m+1)).clip (a.params m).clip (M.alpha N m) O
        (M.stationary N m p F) (Q.Γ j) (Q.c j) (a.clock.loopCap (m+1))

evidence: [M] prints the row/loop/cubic/quartic weighted bounds at w^path_{J_m} with A^path and Lambda^loop_m, plus 'The same bounds hold at w'_{J_m} > w^path_{J_m} > 0 with A' >= A^path', and its proof (C-section.tex:377-416) actually puts A'=A^path and proves the bounds at w' first. [L]'s Planned.cap gives only `(M.path N m).Bounds j.clip j.width j.paths (a.clock.loopCap m)`, and Installed.uses only moves to `σ ≤ i.width` with `i.paths ≤ C`, by narrower (which needs `b ≤ a`). The wider bounds in [L] are hypotheses on intermediate arrays (nextPath/topPath at q.widths.emits/launch, Escrow.emitted for blank-loop classical arrays in the unused Progeny), and they hold only with `q.width i ≤ q.emits j i`, non-strict, so the chosen arrays never get a bound at a strictly larger width. The extra claim is a real statement used in the proof, not a typo.

[M] prints the row, loop and cubic/quartic weighted bounds at w^path with A^path and Lambda^loop for every N and m<=N, and also that the same bounds hold at a larger width w'>w^path with A'>=A^path, uniformly in N; its proof says it chooses w^path<w' and bounds the series at w'. [L]'s Planned.cap gives only `(M.path N m).Bounds j.clip j.width j.paths (a.clock.loopCap m)`, and every other bound on the chosen arrays moves down in width: Installed.uses requires `σ ≤ i.width`, narrower requires `hb : b ≤ a`, and Stationary.launch requires `τ≤σ`. No declaration states Bounds for M.path N m (or Q N m) at a width above (a.params m).width, so the larger-width claim has no counterpart. The proof spells that claim out on purpose, so it is not a typo.
